title: release session brain dump
body:
Quick context:
- Purpose: jot down tactics for a quiet, low-risk canary of model X (xg-1.3b-quant) across Private clusters in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. This is a personal scratchpad — messy, should be cleaned into a formal runbook before next week.

Top-level constraints/assumptions:
- Private deployments: customers may have cold KV caches and different traffic patterns than Hosted. Cannot assume steady-state latency.
- Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated has capacity guarantees; Private may have burstiness and cross-tenant noise.
- Goal: validate correctness + latency tail behavior under small traffic (1-3% global), detect quality regressions on critical prompt set, and verify automatic fallback to smaller model variant.

Canary plan (very rough):
1) Preflight (day -2):
  - Verify build: prod image sha -> tag mapping. Command: curl -sS https://artifact.redwood/api/tags | jq ".[] | select(.tag==\"canary-2026-01-XX\")"
  - Smoke deploy to staging private cluster (staging-eu). Run synthetic test harness (synth-runner v0.5) with 200 short prompts, check token-level diffs.
  - Create datapoints: baseline latency distribution for pinned model v1.3. Record median/p95/p99.

2) Canary rollout (day 0):
  - Phase A (0-60m): route 0.5% of global traffic from a single test client cohort (cohort id=canary-alpha). Observe CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth.
  - Phase B (60-180m): increase to 2% but keep cohort limited to API-key allowlist + 2 internal clients.
  - Phase C (3h+): expand to 5% if no anomalies for 4h.

Safety thresholds (hard stops):
  - latency p99 increase > 40% vs baseline for 15m -> rollback immediate
  - error rate (5xx) > 0.4% for 10m -> rollback
  - quality regressions: BLEU-like prompt set exact-match drop > 1.5% on canary gold prompts -> pause expansion and error budget review
  - GPU OOMs or repeated worker restarts > 3 within 30m -> rollback

Rollback and pinning notes:
- If rollback triggered, pin traffic back to last-known-good model (v1.2.9) via config service: POST /v1/route/pin {route_id, model: \"v1.2.9\", reason} (need to confirm API path)
- Quick pin cheat: edit route yaml in console -> set model_pin: v1.2.9 and set rollout_policy: immediate. Command-to-remember: rbctl routes update --id $ROUTE --pin v1.2.9
- After rollback: collect core dumps, trace logs (trace-id prefix canary-YYYYMMDD), attach to ticket.

Observability checklist (what I need to have in dashboards before launch):
- Per-route token-level cost and latency (median/p95/p99)
- Model-level KV cache hit-rate by cluster and region
- Worker restart events and OOMs over time window
- Request-level payload sizes and prompt length distribution
- Sampling of model outputs (store 1 in 200 requests with redaction) -> run golden prompt eval nightly

Warmup considerations:
- For Private, pre-warm KV cache with common prefixes: run warmup-job with 500 requests mimicking production prompt lengths (especially important for long-history chat workloads).
- Consider ephemeral cache seeding only for clusters below 50% utilization to avoid noisy neighbors.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: does config service accept a soft-rollback (gradual pin over 1h) or only immediate? (ask Platform infra)
- Q: can we automatically throttle canary cohort if SLOs start drifting slowly (e.g., p99 up 10% for 20m)? Implement a throttle webhook?
- TODO: draft a one-pager for CS for customer-facing comms if canary fails and any customers are impacted in Private.
- TODO: add runbook snippet for on-call: exact slack channel, who to page (SRE rotation), and which logs to attach.

Quick ops snippets (for my shell history):
- check canary assignment: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood/api/routes/$ROUTE | jq .canary
- pin route (local cli): rbctl routes update --id $ROUTE --set model_pin=v1.2.9 --reason "auto-rollback"
- fetch recent traces: tracecli query --from -30m --filter "route:$ROUTE and tag:canary" --out traces.json

Notes to self (less formal):
- Keep initial canary tiny. Private customers are scary — we don't get the same telemetry fidelity as Hosted.
- Lean on Priya for the cache-warm approach; she has the warmup job skeleton from the last private rollout.
- Remember to add a short debrief doc after canary: what worked, what surprised, which fallback triggered. Use that to tune Optimize suggestions next sprint.

Post-mortem / debrief template (skeleton):
- Timeline of actions (timestamps)
- Who touched what (deploys, pins, telemetry)
- Metrics before/after (latency, error, quality)
- Root cause and remediation
- Follow-ups (owners + due dates)

Closing: this is messy. Before handoff, turn into a cleaner playbook and add to confluence under eng-release-engineering/canaries. For now — ship small, observe, revert fast.

-- Jordan
